completed: MPI-398 ROOT-CAUSED BY MEASUREMENT and fixed at the source. Both of the card's own hypotheses were WRONG and are recorded as such: POST /wrapper/models/status fired ZERO times in 62s of idle, so MPI-326's storm has not regressed and must not be reopened on this evidence; and EU-RO-1 per-call RTT is fine (~100ms). The real cause: the Pod wrapper runs a SINGLE asyncio loop that also carries the WS pump and the ComfyUI stdout drain, and TWO handlers did multi-second synchronous filesystem work on it, so each one froze every other request. (1) /wrapper/disk ran `du -sb` over a 150GB network volume as a bare subprocess.run, and every concurrent caller spawned a RIVAL walk - polled 6.8/min by the disk bar that self-fed: 1.8s idle -> 32s p50 -> one 125s call Cloudflare 524'd, with /health failing 3 of 4. (2) /wrapper/models/status looped _is_complete_on_disk synchronously over every dep the app sends in one POST (100+ network-FS stats, plus isdir+listdir for node deps), measured ~10s, dragging /wrapper/stats - a 94ms endpoint - to 8693ms. Both are MPI-191's /wrapper/stats fix applied to the endpoints it missed: asyncio.to_thread, plus single-flight behind a lock and a 60s TTL cache for disk (invalidated by _manifest_record_model and models_delete so the bar still tracks a real change). models/status is deliberately NOT cached - install-state feeds the whole download UI and must stay truthful. Wrapper 0.2.38 -> 0.2.40, committed in mpi-ci e760604, R2-floated to the dev channel.

VERIFIED LIVE four ways, each by the same negative control - run the expensive thing and watch whether a cheap neighbour notices. (a) models/check during a real du: 0.45-0.87s vs 0.51-0.96s idle, indistinguishable, where pre-fix it was 0.18s -> 1.37s. (b) 8 concurrent /wrapper/disk: all 200 within 240ms of each other on ONE shared walk, where pre-fix that shape gave 32s p50 and a 524. (c) /remote/pod/stats during two concurrent REAL models/check: 60-97ms, against 8693ms pre-fix. (d) Cold open on a FRESH Pod, user-verified, user's words 'it was instant' against the reported 10-15s blank grid: /health p50 5013ms with 3 of 4 ERR -> p50 141ms 30/30 OK; /wrapper/manifest p50 13714ms -> 282ms; /wrapper/disk p50 32294ms max 125072ms -> p50 371ms; models/status p50 8679ms -> p50 2259ms.

key_decisions: MPI-398 was fixed on the POD, not in the app. The client poll cadence was deliberately left untouched: podDiskBar still runs a 10s interval per mount (js/services/podDiskBar.js:97) and TWO surfaces mount it, but the wrapper's 60s TTL makes the rate harmless, and changing both ends at once would have muddied the attribution. Do not 'finish the job' by throttling the client without a fresh measurement showing it matters.

models/status is deliberately NOT cached, unlike disk. Install-state sits under the entire download UI and correctness there beats one cold scan per Pod boot. If the first-touch cost ever needs to go, the shape is known (cache it the way disk caches du, invalidated by _manifest_record_model / models_delete) - uncarded on purpose, raise it only if a user notices.

/wrapper/ls has the IDENTICAL blocking pattern (du per top-level dir + os.walk) and is worse than either fixed handler, but it has ZERO consumers in routes/ or js/ - manual diagnostic only. Left alone deliberately and recorded, not silently skipped.
The app-side WRAPPER_VERSION floor pin in routes/remotePodLifecycle.js stays at 0.2.36. These are perf fixes, not protocol changes, so an older wrapper must still be accepted.
